# Results

## Study population

A total of $1\,475$ women participated in the OsteoLaus study between 2010 and 2022. After applying study-level exclusion criteria, 2 participants were excluded to not having any match between OsteoLaus and CoLaus as defined in @sec-matching, 48 participants were excluded because of missing examination dates, and 188 participants that had only one visit time point (@fig-consort).

For the HGS analysis, 29 participants were excluded because they had fewer than two study visits available after accounting for missing covariates and out-of-range values. The final analytical sample therefore included $1\,186$ participants. For the ALMI analysis, the 108 participants were excluded for the same reasons resulting in $1\,007$. For GS, 368 participants met the requirement of having at least two study visits and were included in the analysis. This resulted in 829 participants in the final dataset

For the EWGSOP2 sarcopenia incidence analysis, 24 participants with sarcopenia at T1 were excluded. An additional 28 participants were excluded because they had fewer than two study visits, resulting in a final sample of $1\,163$ participants. For the alternative sarcopenia definition FNIH, 14 participants were sarcopenic at T1 and 107 participants had only one visiting time point thus were excluded.

![](images/consort_flow-01.png){#fig-consort}

Most participants included in the HGS analysis contributed data from at least 3 of the 3 possible time points (mean 76.9% of participants). For GS, all participants had exactly two visits, as gait speed was measured at only two time points and the inclusion criterion required data from both visits. For ALMI, most participants contributed data from XX of the 3 possible study visits.

## Dataset matching

@fig-timepoint_dist shows the distribution of examination date differences between matched CoLaus and OsteoLaus visits. For T1 and T2, CoLaus assessments generally occurred before the corresponding OsteoLaus visits, with median differences of 254 and 276 days, respectively. For T3, CoLaus assessments more frequently occurred after the matched OsteoLaus visit, with a median difference of 175 days.

![](images/clipboard-2572005451.png){#fig-timepoint_dist fig-align="left"}

Detailed distribution of missingness over time points can be found in Supplementary Table XX for complete case and Supplementary Figure XX for imputed dataset.

A total of 10 multiply imputed datasets were generated. Diagnostic plots showed mostly good convergence of the imputation models and similar distributions between observed and imputed values (Supplementary Figure XX).

For the baseline variables of left/right arm lean mass, left/right leg lean mass, convergence showed a trend.

## Association between dairy intake and handgrip strength

Handgrip was modelled with a random intercept and random slop. Looking at the data visually showed slightly different sloped per participants over time and comparing a model with and without random slope showed a smaller AIC and BIC for random slope.

\*visualize picture

The models assumption of normality, homoc... were all met

\*graphs

The model fit was as follows: \*Formula

Table 3 shows the key findings of the linear mixed-effects models. Each additional 100g of dairy is associated with a 0.23 kg increase in HGS, independent of other factors. Other significant predictors of HGS are age at T1 (β = -2.92, 95% CI: XX, p\<0.001) and time since T1 (β = -0.11, p\<0.001). **The between-person effect showed t**hat for every 10-year difference in age at baseline, older participants started with approx. 2.9 kg less HGS than younger participants. **The within-person effect showed** that as an individual stays in the study, they lose about 0.11 kg of grip strength per year. Being a former smoker is associated with higher HGS compared to never-smokers (β = 0.70, p=0.03) but current smoker is not.

- For BMI category **(Normal, Overweight, Obese),** all are significant and positive compared to the reference ("Underweight"). Being Overweight has the largest positive association (β = +2.43) with HGS.

The other variables are not significantly associated with change in HGS.
